hypothesis: H2 engineering integration; no general scientific status upgrade
runtime: @earendil-works/pi-durable1.4.0, chord1.4.0, Node24.19.0 Windows x64, native Node SQLite
caller: Optional openService adapter over actual Harness.createConversation/commit/task scheduler and file-backed native SqliteStorage. Two logical client conversations in one durable Session/database; three sequential OS processes.
workload: Six admitted custom native tasks: four intended local transactional document effects, one admission followed by permission revocation before effect, one cancellation before effect. A two-slot shared budget rejects overload; duplicates/conflicts/obsolete authority versions are checked. Kill two processes after separate effect+checkpoint commits and before their terminal phases, then reopen twice and prove progress after each boundary.
integration: Real Harness/Session/TaskRuntime/registry/SQLite, custom task phase handlers and host admission/authority adapter. No mock scheduler, no GenerationTask, model, provider, network, external tool or tenant authentication endpoint.
bottleneck: Bounded live-work admission and recovery of committed effects/checkpoints without duplicate local writes; no benchmark or scale throughput claim.
acceptance: All three subprocesses use the same pinned executable/runtime and three distinct actual PIDs. First two are actually terminated by the controller; final process closes normally with exit0. No retry after any failed boundary.
Stage0: two live tasks; overload rejected; duplicate reuses task identity; revoked conversation's effect denied inside the current commit; only effect-one committed and held before first crash.

Stage1: same task/effect identities recovered in paused scheduler; obsolete admission denied; first task finishes, second effect committed and held; native abort settles pre-effect cancellation; freed capacity admits effect-progress, which finishes before second crash.

Stage2: original request identities deduplicate; changed payload conflicts; second task finishes; effect-final admitted/completed after second restart; zero active tasks, all six terminal, four effects count1, denied/cancelled effects absent.

Observed application-document publications have strictly increasing sequence values and never exceed two active admissions. Their final sequence/value equals the retained SQLite document revision and exported final snapshot; current-only session checkpoints compact prior revisions, so this does not claim independent complete historical commit coverage. Twelve observed admission calls comprise six admitted, three duplicates, one overload, one stale-authority refusal and one payload conflict. Independent Python SQLite reads retain integrityok and six expected native task records.

Workload completion/rejection/denial/cancellation denominators, stage elapsed time, worker OS-reported usage and parent-observed process memory recorded descriptively. Injected gate/IO costs are included; no unobserved peak, causal observer overhead, tail-throughput or production extrapolation.
failure_policy: Stop at the first error/deadline/resource ceiling, retain outputs and exit receipts, do not edit frozen sources or retry. Missing later stages remain unexecuted. Post-outcome receipt inspection is preservation, not execution acceptance.
limits: One Windows host, two conversations in a single durable Session; trusted-host authority versions and SQLite-transaction effects only. No external-provider exactly-once guarantee, concurrent writer authority, independent tenants, GenerationTask/submission11635 reproduction, GPU, distributed or production validation. Request-history grows with accepted requests; only live admission is bounded. Historical H2 gaps/H1 failures and unchanged5GiB H1 gate remain.
